label: monk2-s0
summary: This MONK-2 model predicts yes when a1 = 3, or when at most three of the six attributes take their first value; that rule agrees with the model on 418 of the 432 input combinations. Two parts do the work: a hidden counter of attributes away from their first value (a2, a3, a4, a6, with a bonus for a1 = 2), shut off by a1 = 3, which pushes cases with several non-first values to yes (switching it off drops the score-based training AUC from 0.734 to 0.537); and direct per-level scores in which a1 = 3 counts strongly for yes and a1 = 1 and a5 = 1 strongly against (off: 0.599). An a3/a5 gate and an a6 flag are minor. The model has learned only the "not too many first values" side of the target concept (exactly two first values): it says yes on every cell where that concept does (0 misses) and on 229 further cells, so it over-predicts yes: mean predicted risk 84.7% against an outcome rate of 32.8% on the 345 training rows, training accuracy 47.2%.
